members.name: Dahlia Malkhi
members.bio: Dahlia Malkhi is a Professor in the Department of Computer Science of UCSB since 2024 and the Founding head of the fftech lab. Malkhi serves as Distinguished Scientist of Chainlink Labs, advisor of Espresso Systems, advisor of nubit.org, advisor of SpaceCoin, former CTO at the Diem Association, and former Lead Researcher at Novi Financial. Her research over two decades spans broad aspects of reliability and security of distributed systems, recently with focus on blockchains and advances in financial technology. Her work resulted in over 200 publications as well as a strong impact on computing technology.

members.name: Maofan "Ted" Yin
members.bio: Ted Yin is co-founder of Ava Labs, a co-author of the HotStuff protocol, and the main driver of Cordwood.

members.name: Kali Hale
members.bio: Kali Hale started her graduate studies in computer science at UCSB in fall of 2022 and was accepted to the PhD program in fall of 2024. She graduated from California Lutheran University with her BS in Computer Science in May 2022.

members.name: Rithwik Kerur
members.bio: Rithwik Kerur started his PhD studies in the Computer Science department of UCSB in the fall of 2024. He graduated from UC Irvine in 2024 with a bachelors in Computer Science, and is interested in distributed systems, distributed computing, financial markets, and data management.

members.name: Shaunak Umarkhedi
members.bio: Shaunak Umarkhedi started his PhD studies in Computer Science at UC Santa Barbara in Fall 2026. His research interests include distributed systems, confidential computing, and security.

members.name: Maksym Ioffe
members.bio: Maksym Ioffe started his PhD studies in Computer Science at UC Santa Barbara in Fall 2026. He graduated from Cornell University with a bachelor's degree in Computer Science. His research interests include distributed systems, consensus protocols, and applied cryptography.

members.name: Kaiyang Chang
members.bio: Kaiyang is a Master's student in Computer Science at UCSB, where he works with Professor Dahlia Malkhi. His research interests lie at the intersection of blockchain, cryptography, and decentralized finance, with a focus on central limit order books (CLOBs), secure multi-party computation (MPC), smart contracts, and zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). Before UCSB, Kaiyang earned a B.S. in Computer Science from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI), where he conducted research with Professor Oshani Seneviratne in the BRAINS Lab on decentralized systems and blockchain technologies.

members.name: Neil Roy
members.bio: Neil Roy is a Master's student in the Computer Science department at UCSB. His research is focused on Web3 development, specifically decentralized systems, cryptography, consensus mechanisms, and peer-to-peer network design.

members.name: Javin Zipkin
members.bio: Javin Zipkin is a BS/MS student in Computer Science, graduating with his masters in 2026. He advanced with his B.S. in Computer Science from UCSB in 2025. Javin is engaged with Fftech and the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) in research on Private Information Retrieval (PIR). Javin is interested in distributed systems, databases, and computational musicology.

members.name: Sawyer Rice
members.bio: Sawyer Rice started his MS studies in the Computer Science department of UCSB in the winter of 2026. He graduated from UCSB in fall of 2025 with a bachelors in Computer Science, and is interested in distributed systems and databases.

members.name: Ruslan Akhtariev
members.bio: Ruslan Akhtariev is an undergraduate student in UCSB and a Web3 developer in Cosmos, Ethereum and Solana ecosystems. Ruslan is the President at the Blockchain@UCSB club. His interests include distributed systems, cryptography and finance.

members.name: Parth Mahajan
members.bio: Parth Mahajan is an undergraduate student at UCSB, double-majoring in Economics & Accounting and Statistics & Data Science. He has been active in crypto markets and DeFi research since 2020. His interests include cross-chain settlement, stablecoin infrastructure, and distributed systems.

members.name: Tom Shangguan
members.bio: Tom Shangguan was a master's student in the Computer Science department at UCSB. His interests include distributed systems, databases, and memory management. He is working on optimizing authenticated data structures—data structures that enable users to verify integrity and authenticity via cryptographic proofs without full data access—to produce smaller proofs for frequently accessed contents.

members.name: Kevin Chang
members.bio: Kevin was an undergraduate student in UCSB. He received his bachelor's degree in UCSB's Department of Applied Mathematics. His interests include distributed systems, AI, and finance.

members.name: Ysabel Chen
members.bio: Ysabel Chen received her bachelor's degree in UCSB's Department of Computer Science. She was the President at Blockchain@UCSB club and has authored a paper debating blockchain regulation. Her interests include distributed systems, finance, and aerospace.

members.name: Nir Chemaya
members.bio: Nir Chemaya received his PhD in Economics in 2025. Chemaya focuses on innovations in the Fintech markets, such as blockchain and Decentralized Finance (DeFi), and agents' interactions with those technologies. He has authored several papers on Decentralized Exchanges and possesses extensive knowledge of blockchain technologies and payment systems. Chemaya was also one of the leaders of the UCSB-ECON DeFi Seminar, a graduate-student-led seminar series sponsored by Uniswap.
